source.title: The dynorphin/kappa opioid system as a modulator of stress-induced and pro-addictive behaviors

confidence_rationale: Well-cited review consolidating the dynorphin/KOR-as-aversive-state-controller account: KOR activation produces dysphoria, potentiates drug-seeking and stress-induced reinstatement, and operates downstream of CRF. Grounds the layer's premise that there is a dedicated neuropeptide system whose job is to install/modulate negative affective state -- the substrate for a distinct vulnerability axis. Confidence mid-range because it is a review (synthesis, not primary), and as with Land 2008 the 'commitment-entropy' reading is REE's, not the literature's.
failure_signatures: The review frames dynorphin/KOR around dysphoria and addiction/relapse, not commitment or option-selection; it gives no independent support for the 'raises policy entropy' half of the layer's claim beyond the affective-state framing.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The endogenous dynorphin/kappa-opioid-receptor system modulates mood and increases the rewarding effects of abused drugs; its activation plays a major role in the pro-addictive effects of stress, mediating dysphoria, potentiating drug-seeking, and driving stress-induced reinstatement, in tight interaction with the CRF system; KOR antagonists are highlighted as candidate therapeutics for affective dysregulation.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports the layer's Section 3C premise that there is a dedicated system whose function is to set negative affective/aversive state -- the kappa pole of the commitment-entropy axis (opposing the mu stabiliser, MECH-048). The CRF-dynorphin coupling and the therapeutic framing of KOR antagonism ground the prediction (PHARM-018) that kappa antagonism normalises pathological aversive-state-lock.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Review-level synthesis centred on dysphoria and addiction/relapse, not on commitment or policy-selection dynamics. It corroborates the 'aversive-state controller' substrate but provides no independent evidence for the specific 'raises policy entropy / destabilises commitments' computational claim.
mapping.source_context: Rodent-dominated mechanistic review; stress, mood, addiction.

confidence_components.notes: Solid consolidating review by the leading group. Mapping_fidelity moderate (aversive-state substrate well grounded; commitment-entropy construct not). Partly overlaps Land 2008 (same group) -- included as the synthesis/therapeutic-framing complement rather than independent primary data.
